The authors suggested monitoring indices of bone health, optimising lifestyle factors, maintaining vitamin D and calcium status, and preventing falls in patients on long-term therapy. Despite these alterations in bone metabolism reports of clinical osteomalacia associated with antiepileptics are rare.13 A study in 20 epileptic outpatients who had received antiepileptic therapy for a mean of 14 ⁄ years failed to show any clinical evidence of osteomalacia although there was some evidence of altered calci- um metabolism.14 Similarly osteomalacia was seen in only 1 of 19 elderly inpatients in another study,15 a rate similar to that pre- viously seen in elderly patients with acute illness not receiving antiepileptic therapy. 1.
